Context/Background: ASXL1 plays key roles in epigenetic regulation of early developmental gene expression. De novo protein-truncating mutations in ASXL1 cause Bohring-Opitz syndrome (BOS), a rare neurodevelopmental condition characterized by severe intellectual disabilities, distinctive facial features, hypertrichosis, increased risk of Wilms tumor, and variable congenital anomalies, including heart defects and severe skeletal defects giving rise to a typical BOS posture. These BOS-causing ASXL1 variants are also high-prevalence somatic driver mutations in acute myeloid leukemia.  We used primary cells from individuals with BOS (n = 18) and controls (n = 49) to dissect gene regulatory changes caused by ASXL1 mutations using comprehensive multiomics assays for chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), DNA methylation, histone methylation binding, and transcriptome in peripheral blood and skin fibroblasts.
Prompt: Based on the results of the blood and fibroblast transcriptomic DEG analyses of BOS vs controls, provide a discussion of the common and distinct pathways found between blood and fibroblast and any relevance to the presence in the BOS samples of ASXL1 truncating mutations.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
ASXL1 truncating mutations cause Bohring-Opitz syndrome (BOS), a severe neurodevelopmental disorder with somatic overlap in acute myeloid leukemia. We performed RNA-seq on primary peripheral blood (n = 18 BOS vs n = 49 controls) and skin fibroblasts (same individuals) to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Fibroblast DEG analysis (Table S11) yielded 999 genes at padj < 0.05; blood (Table S12) yielded 2,118. We applied preranked GSEA (log2FoldChange) across KEGG_2016, GO_Biological_Process_2023, Reactome_Pathways_2024 and MSigDB_Hallmark_2020. Details not specified in file metadata.

Keywords  
• Epigenetic regulation  
• Neuronal development/axon guidance  
• Inflammatory response  
• PI3K-Akt signaling  
• Synaptic transmission  

Candidate Genes  
ASXL1 (epigenetic regulator)  
CBX2 (Polycomb chromatin factor)  
CNTN4 (neuronal adhesion)  
GRIK5 (glutamate receptor)  
VANGL2 (planar cell polarity)  

Pathway Enrichments  

Fibroblasts (GSEA preranked by log2FC)  
Counts by database:  
• KEGG_2016: 0 UP, 1 DOWN (100% down)  
• GO_Biological_Process_2023: 4 UP, 2 DOWN (67% up)  
• Reactome_Pathways_2024: 0 UP, 1 DOWN (100% down)  

KEGG_2016 (DOWN)  
| Theme                    | Direction | Leading Genes                            |  
| PI3K-Akt signaling       | Down      | IL7, TLR4, PPP2R2B, LAMC1, IL4R         |  

GO_Biological_Process_2023 (UP)  
| Theme                                    | Direction | Leading Genes                       |  
| Axon Guidance (GO:0007411)               | Up        | CNTN4                               |  
| Neuron Projection Guidance (GO:0097485)  | Up        | CNTN4                               |  
| Axonogenesis (GO:0007409)                | Up        | CNTN4                               |  
| Chemical Synaptic Transmission (GO:0007268) | Up     | CHRM3, APBA2, GRIK5, GRID1          |  

GO_Biological_Process_2023 (DOWN)  
| Theme                                               | Direction | Leading Genes               |  
| Cellular Response To Oxygen-Containing Compound      | Down      | SIRPA, TLR4, CLU, CPNE7    |

| Theme          | Direction | Leading Genes                                           |  
| Immune System  | Down      | SIRPA, NPDC1, IL7, CLU, TLR4, SLC2A5, IFI27, SOCS2, IL4R |  

Analysis  
Fibroblasts with ASXL1 truncations show pronounced up-regulation of neuronal‐development programs (axon guidance, synaptic transmission) and concomitant down-regulation of PI3K–Akt signaling and innate immune pathways.   This suggests loss of ASXL1 disrupts chromatin controls over developmental gene networks in somatic fibroblasts, echoing its role in early embryonic patterning.

Blood (preranked GSEA)

| Complement                         | Down      | CFH, CTSS, S100A9, CXCL1, LYN     |  

Analysis  
Blood from BOS patients shows a strong skew toward down-regulated inflammatory and innate-immune programs (e.g., phagosome, NF-κB/TNF/TLR pathways) alongside up-regulated ribosomal and heme-scavenging functions. A smaller neurodevelopmental signature (nervous system development) also emerges. This contrasts with fibroblasts, where neuronal pathways are dominant and immune programs suppressed.  

Targeted (keyword-guided) subset  
• Fibroblast CNTN4‐driven GSEA: Axon Guidance (GO:0007411) leads with CNTN4.  
• Blood inflammation subset: Inflammatory Response (GO:0006954) leads with MEFV, IFNG, IL1B, TLR2, CXCL8.  

Key Genes/Proteins (leading‐edge)  

Up‐regulated  
| Gene  | Direction     | Role/Function               | Pathway(s)                              |  
|-------|---------------|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------------|  
| CNTN4 | Fibro UP      | Neuronal cell adhesion      | Axon Guidance; Neuron Projection Guidance; Axonogenesis |  
| CHRM3 | Fibro UP      | Muscarinic acetylcholine receptor | Chemical Synaptic Transmission    |  

Down‐regulated  
| Gene  | Direction     | Role/Function                    | Pathway(s)                                |  
|-------|---------------|----------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|  
| SIRPA | Fibro DOWN    | Macrophage inhibitory receptor    | Immune System; Cellular Response to Oxygen Compound |  
| IL1B  | Blood DOWN    | Pro-inflammatory cytokine         | Inflammatory Response; Cytokine Signaling in Immune System |  

Comparisons  
– Common trend: suppression of immune-inflammatory modules in BOS samples.  
– Distinct: fibroblasts specifically activate neuronal development programs; blood uniquely exhibits ribosomal/heme metabolism and extensive down-regulation of innate-immune signaling.  

Implications  
These findings align with ASXL1’s role in epigenetic modulation of developmental loci: truncating mutations may derepress neuronal gene networks in fibroblasts while impairing immune-gene activation in blood. Such dysregulation could underlie BOS neurodevelopmental features and increased susceptibility to hematologic malignancy.  

Next Steps & Clarifications  
1. Validate PI3K-Akt signaling down-regulation at the protein level in fibroblasts.  
2. Map ASXL1 and CBX2 occupancy at key neuronal and immune loci (ChIP-seq).  
3. Compare transcriptomic shifts with AML samples harboring ASXL1 truncations.  
4. Assess functional cytokine responses in BOS patient blood cells.
